thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO breach detected - streaming route /v1/stream (eu-west-1) p95 and p99 spiking. p95=1.2s -> 2.0s, p99=0.9s -> 4.2s. Error rate low but tail latency > SLO. Paging oncall @oncall-alex

oncall-alex: I'm looking. Do we have a quick grafana link?

maria: grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams/stream-latency?orgId=1&from=-15m (chart shows sharp p99 jump at 13:02 UTC). Also saw a few customer tickets: customers A, C, and a transcription partner reporting stalled responses.

samir: grabbing proxy logs from the ALB->ingress proxy path. Early sign: a lot of long-lived connections with small chunk writes; proxy write buffer shows "buffered_chunk" events and occasional "socket.close after write".

derek: can you paste a sample proxy log line?

samir: sure, tail -n 200 proxy.log | grep stream-route | tail -20

```
2024-11-02T13:02:11.123Z proxy[ingress-12] INFO route=/v1/stream client=10.2.3.4 req_id=abc123 state=chunk_bufed size=64 flush_ms=0
2024-11-02T13:02:12.456Z proxy[ingress-12] WARN route=/v1/stream client=10.2.3.4 req_id=abc123 state=socket.write err=broken_pipe
2024-11-02T13:02:13.789Z proxy[ingress-12] INFO route=/v1/stream client=10.2.3.5 req_id=def456 state=chunk_bufed size=8 flush_ms=1200
```

derek: looks like write batching in the proxy is accumulating tiny chunks and only flushing on thresholds or timeouts. That would increase tail latency when clients backpressure or slow-read. Did we recently change the chunk flush config?

maria: yes—yesterday we rolled out a change to the ingress proxy to improve throughput for small non-streaming responses: default_flush_interval=300ms -> 800ms to reduce syscalls. That could explain worse tail for streaming. Rollout was to 50% of traffic.

samir: confirming rollout flags: ingress-proxy v2.8.1 -> rollout=50% since 03:00 UTC.

oncall-alex: ok that correlates. For immediate mitigation, can we revert the flush interval or enable per-route streaming flush policy for /v1/stream?

derek: we can. Two quick options: 1) flip the feature flag for streaming routes to force immediate flush (recommended), or 2) short-term revert the global change (more blast radius). I'd prefer per-route override.

maria: rolling a per-route config patch now. snippet: 
```yaml
route /v1/stream:
  chunk_flush_interval_ms: 50
  disable_gzip: true
```

maria: deploying to the ingress canary (10% traffic) now.

oncall-alex: Samir, can you watch connection metrics and p95/p99? I'll update oncall rotation.

samir: watching. Also enabling proxy debug logging for chunking only to gather more traces (low overhead).

```bash
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/ingress-proxy PROXY_CHUNK_DEBUG=1 --record
kubectl -n infra rollout status deploy/ingress-proxy -w
```

samir: canary config applied. Observability: within 30s the canary p99 dropped from ~4s -> ~0.9s for that shard.

derek: good sign. Maria, can you push the per-route override to 100%? Also disable gzip for streaming since compression buffers can add latency.

maria: pushing to 100% now. Patch rolled to 100% at the ingress layer.

oncall-alex: update: p95 back to ~0.45s, p99 ~0.95s across eu-west. We'll keep monitoring.

cs-bot: customer-impact digest: 14 customers reported degraded streaming UX in the last hour; 3 filed support tickets, 1 escalated. No data loss reported; only increased latency/tail.

derek: root cause candidate: rollout of increased flush interval aimed at reducing syscall overhead for small responses inadvertently increased chunk coalescing for streaming endpoints. Interaction with gzip and slow-reading clients exacerbated tail.

samir: additional note: some client SDKs send small early frames (10-50 bytes) expecting immediate flush—those were buffered. Also saw occasional ALB idle timeouts closing connections after buffered writes, producing broken_pipe errors. ALB keepalive configured to 60s; proxy had longer idle setting.

oncall-alex: mitigation summary for handoff: 
- Immediate: per-route chunk_flush_interval_ms=50 and disable_gzip for all streaming routes (done)
- Short-term: revert global flush interval rollout until we have safe defaults (ops runbook task)
- Medium: add test harness for streaming microbench (simulate slow-read clients) and integrate into CI
- Long-term: telemetry: add per-request chunk latency histograms and an alert for cluster-wide chunk flush time > 200ms

oncall-alex: handing off to kate for monitoring and postmortem at shift change. Kate, please take it from here and own the postmortem link.

kate: on it. I will keep a watch for the next 4 hours, updating every 30m or on regression. Creating postmortem doc now: https://docs.redwood.example/postmortems/1728004321-streaming-chunk-flush.json

kate: initial customer impact assessment: P1 -> downgraded to P2 after mitigation since no data loss and latency restored within SLO envelope for most customers. Affected customers list added to postmortem.

oncall-alex: good. Follow-ups assigned: SAMIR (collect debug logs and TTL), MARIA (revert global rollout + plan canary), DEREK (CI streaming test), KATE (postmortem + customer comms).

maria: created PR for rollback of global flush change: https://git.redwood.example/r/proxy/merge/3141

samir: uploaded collected proxy traces and associated request ids to the incident storage.

kate: leaving handoff notes in incident tracker. If anyone sees p99 drift again re-ping with @oncall-alex.

incident-bot: Incident incident-1728004321 status=mitigated severity=P2 owner=kate slack_channel=incidents

kate: closing thread for active mitigation; will reopen for postmortem review comments.
